site.title: SurveyReview
site.subtitle: A Reviewer-Aligned Benchmark for Survey Evaluators
site.announcement: The current website ships with the anonymized test version from the repository. You can point the dataset button to Hugging Face later without touching the page layout.

overview.intro: SurveyReview evaluates whether a model can judge survey-style academic writing the way a reviewer would. Instead of measuring generic summarization quality, it scores review-oriented decisions across readability, criticalness, comprehensiveness, and structure, and also tracks the quality of generated reasoning with an RQS judge.
highlights: Reviewer-aligned labels over four concrete survey-review dimensions.
An anonymized test release that is already runnable with the included evaluation pipeline.
A lightweight API-based evaluator plus a separate reason-quality judge.
A leaderboard format that reports both score prediction quality and reasoning quality.

dimensions.name: Readability
dimensions.description: Measures overall clarity and ease of understanding in the manuscript presentation.

dimensions.name: Criticalness
dimensions.description: Measures whether the manuscript offers new insights, meaningful critique, or depth beyond a surface-level recap.

dimensions.name: Comprehensiveness
dimensions.description: Measures whether references are complete, relevant, and sufficient for a solid survey.

dimensions.name: Structure
dimensions.description: Measures the logical flow and coherence across sections and subsections.

pipeline.title: Load survey excerpts
pipeline.description: The evaluator reads anonymized article text from the current repository release and pairs each UID with dimension-specific labels.

pipeline.title: Predict reviewer scores
pipeline.description: A target model receives the dimension prompt and the survey text, then must output brief reasoning plus a discrete score from the benchmark scale.

pipeline.title: Judge the reasoning
pipeline.description: A second model scores the quality of the predicted reasoning against the reference comments, producing the reported RQS metric.

examples.title: Survey of Scientific Rigor Studied in Machine Learning
examples.summary: A representative low-score readability case where reviewers wanted the paper to make its audience and contribution substantially clearer.
reasons: Who is the audience is meant to be and what is the paper trying to tell that audience?
Because the intended audience is muddied, it is also unclear what the takeaway from the paper is.
I would like to see this paper make clearer what its contribution and audience are.

examples.title: The nutritional status of children living within institutionalized care: a systematic review
examples.summary: A positive criticalness example where the reviewer credits the paper for surfacing gaps and directions for future work.
reasons: The discussion section provides us with main gaps and new directions.
The manuscript highlights the continuing challenge of malnutrition among children in institutionalized care.
The review also points out that the area still needs more rigorous studies.

examples.title: Community-level dietary intake of sodium, potassium, and sodium-to-potassium ratio as a global public health problem
examples.summary: A typical comprehensiveness issue where reviewers ask for missing regions, missing comparisons, or broader coverage of prior evidence.
reasons: Why no studies from South America or Canada were included in analysis?
Kindly provide in Discussion section data from WHO on Na, K intake and compare that to your data?

examples.title: The nutritional status of children living within institutionalized care: a systematic review
examples.summary: A low-score structure example where the reviewer calls out section ordering and paragraph flow rather than scientific contribution.
reasons: Lines 141-157 could be rephrased and may be broken into two paragraphs.
Lines 170-189 read more like methods and may be better moved after improving the flow.
The authors may consider shifting this section to the methods section after improving its flow.

usage: Edit docs/data/benchmark.json to replace the current GitHub dataset URL with your Hugging Face dataset URL when it is ready.
Update the leaderboard array in the same JSON file whenever you have new scores; the table is rendered automatically.
If you later get a public paper URL, fill in site.paperUrl and the Paper button will appear by itself.
Deploy the docs folder with GitHub Pages; detailed steps are in docs/DEPLOY.md.
releaseNote: This page is intentionally data-driven. Most future edits should be simple content swaps inside docs/data/benchmark.json rather than HTML or CSS changes.
